question: How is a bound being situated among the yoginī group designated in the Kula tradition?
premises: A being is situated in the midst of the yoginī group.
That being is identified as a paśu.
This designation is stated within the Kula tradition.
inference: In the Kula tradition, one situated in the midst of the yoginī group is called a paśu.
plain_english: In the Kula tradition, he who is situated in the midst of the group of yoginīs is called a paśu.
